title: τίθημι, ἀφίημι, δείκνυμι, ἀπόλλυμι
description: The μι verbs τίθημι, ἀφίημι, δείκνυμι and ἀπόλλυμι, ὥστε with the accusative and infinitive, and the subjunctive after ἕως.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html:
τίθημι, I place, has the principal parts τίθημι, θήσω, ἔθηκα, τέθεικα, τέθειμαι, ἐτέθην. The stem is θε-. The present system is reduplicated like δίδωμι (τιθε-); the aorist active is first aorist with κ in the indicative (ἔθηκα) and second aorist in the other moods (θῶ, θές, θεῖναι, θείς). The perfect lengthens θε- to θει-, and the aorist passive changes θε- to τε- (ἐτέθην) so that two θ's do not stand in successive syllables. The participles τιθείς and θείς are declined like λυθείς. In a middle form, τιθε- marks the present system and θε- alone the second aorist: ἀνεθέμην is a second aorist, ἐτίθεντο an imperfect.

ἀφίημι, I let go, I permit, I leave, I forgive, is ἀπό + ἵημι (stem ἑ-): ἰ- before the stem marks the present system, and the short forms with ἑ- alone are second aorist (ἀφείς, like θείς). The indicative has a κ aorist: ἀφῆκα. When it means forgive, it takes the accusative of the thing and the dative of the person: ἀφίημί σοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας.

δείκνυμι, I show, and ἀπόλλυμι, I destroy (middle, I perish), add some present endings straight to a stem in υ (δείκνυμι, ἀπολλύμεθα), but are also conjugated like ω verbs (δεικνύω, ἀπολλύω).

ὥστε, so that, can take the accusative and infinitive of result: ὥστε τὸν ὄχλον θαυμάσαι, so that the crowd marvelled. ἕως ἄν (or ἕως οὗ) with the subjunctive means until, of something still to come: ἴσθι ἐκεῖ ἕως ἂν εἴπω σοι, stay there until I tell you; of an actual past event it takes the indicative.

θῶ, θῇς, θῇ, θῶμεν, θῆτε, θῶσι(ν)
The middle: present τίθεμαι, imperfect ἐτιθέμην; aorist ἐθέμην, ἔθου, ἔθετο; participle θέμενος.

blocks.caption: Common confusion
blocks.html: θῇ (he may place) and θῇς come from τίθημι; θῆτε (you may place) is not a form of θέλω. ἔθηκα is an aorist even though it has κ; the perfect is τέθεικα. ἀφίημι keeps its rough breathing hidden in the φ of ἀφ-: ἀφῆκεν, he left or he forgave; ἀφέντες, having left. ὥστε (so that) differs from ὥσπερ (just as). ἕως with the genitive is up to, until; as a conjunction it is while, until.
